chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Dawud, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah! I have dependents and a debt upon me, and my situation has become difficult, so teach me a supplication with which I will call upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to provide me with what I can pay off my debt with and assist me with my dependents.'

So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'O servant of Allah! Perform ablution and perfect your ablution, then pray two cycles, completing the bowing and prostration, then say.'

'O Glorified, O One, O Benevolent, O Eternal! I turn to You by Muhammad, Your Prophet, the Prophet of Mercy (peace be upon him and his family). O Muhammad, O Messenger of Allah! I turn by You to Allah, your Lord and my Lord and the Lord of everything, that You send blessings upon Muhammad and his Household; and I ask You for a noble breath from Your breaths, and an easy breakthrough, and a wide sustenance, with which I gather my scattered affairs and pay off my debt and assist me with my dependents.'
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for relieving debt and providing sustenance according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith highlights the Shia emphasis on intercession (tawassul) through the Prophet and his Ahl al-Bayt as a means of accessing divine grace. The prescribed ritual combines physical purification with spiritual connection, illustrating how practical acts of worship are integrated with specific invocations to resolve worldly hardships like debt and family support.
